The defendant No.1 in O.S.No.227/1993 on the file of the III Addl. Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Belgaum (hereinafter referred to as the 'trial Court' for short) has filed this regular second appeal challenging the judgment and decree dated 07.07.2006 by the Additional District Judge and Fast Track-IV Court, Belgaum (hereinafter referred to as the 'First Appellate Court' for short) in R.A.No.91/2002.
2.

The parties shall henceforth be referred to as they were arrayed before the trial Court.
3.
The suit in O.S.No.227/1993 was filed for recovery of a sum of Rs.62,000/- with interest.
The plaintiffs claim that plaintiff No.1 was the father and plaintiff No.2 was the cousin of defendant No.2.
The defendant No.1 is the husband of defendant No.2.
It was claimed that during the pregnancy of defendant No.2, she developed complications and had to undergo medical procedures at KLE Hospital, Belagavi and Wanloss Hospital, Miraj.
On oral request of defendant No.1, plaintiffs spent Rs.62,000/- for treatment of defendant No.2.
They claimed that the defendant No.1 agreed to pay the NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 amount within few days, but he failed to keep up his promise.
The plaintiffs caused a notice dated 19.06.1991 despite which, the defendant No.1 did not pay the amount.
Hence, the plaintiff filed the suit to recover the said sum.

4. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1 who contended that the defendant No.2 had deserted the matrimonial home without any just cause and she in collusion with the plaintiffs had filed a criminal case against him alleging an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC and also filed a petition under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C., claiming maintenance.
He contended that in order to harass him, the present suit is filed.

He also claimed that the treatment and the other procedures undergone by the defendant No.2 were not to his notice and therefore, contended that he was not liable to pay the amount as claimed by the plaintiffs.

5. Based on these contentions, the trial Court framed the following issues:
"1] Whether the plaintiffs prove that the defendant No.2 during her pregnancy, was admitted in Hospital at Belgaum and then at Miraj for treatment and operation as alleged?

and operation of defendant No.2 as alleged?
3] Whether the plaintiffs prove that the defendant No.1 assured to pay the said sum as alleged?

sentences.text: 4] Whether the defendant No.1 proves that he is entitled for compensatory costs of Rs.10,000/- as contended?
5] Are the plaintiffs entitled for the amount as sought for?
6] To what order or Decree?"
6 . The GPA holder of the plaintiff No.1 was examined as PW1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P63.
An elderly person known to both plaintiffs and the defendant was examined as PW2.

The defendant No.1 was examined as DW1.
7.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the trial Court held that there is nothing to establish that the defendant No.1 had agreed to pay the cost of treatment of the defendant No.2 and therefore, held that there was no contractual liability on the part of the defendant No.1 to pay the amount allegedly spent by the plaintiffs for the treatment of the defendant No.2.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree, the plaintiffs filed R.A.No.91/2002.

The First Appellate Court secured the records of the trial Court and heard the counsel for the parties and framed the following points for its consideration:
"1.
Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to recover the suit claim from defendant-1 towards medical expenses of defendant-2?
2. Whether the impugned judgment suffers any illegality and is liable to be set aside?
3. What order?"
9. The First Appellate Court held that the relationship between the defendants was strained only after 1992-93 and it is only thereafter that matrimonial cases were filed against each other.

It noted that in the reply issued by defendant No.1 to the notice issued by the plaintiffs, he stated that the defendant No.2 met him at Khade Bazar, Belgaum and took his signatures on some blank forms stating that it is required for some medical treatment.
It also noted that defendant No.1 did not spend anything towards the treatment of defendant No.2 after the marriage.

It held that the documents produced before the Court demonstrated beyond doubt that the plaintiffs had NC:
2024:KHC-D:3206 proved that defendant No.2 was admitted in hospitals at Belgaum and Miraj for treatment and operation.

It held that the trial Court too had noticed this and therefore, held that the Shivaji Yellappa Astekar vs Sri Annasaheb Ramachandra Kawale on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44568634/
4 medical procedures undergone by the defendant No.2 were admitted.

sentences.text: Therefore, the First Appellate Court held that when the plaintiff had proved the expenses incurred, the defendant No.1 being the husband of defendant No.2 was bound to pay the cost.

Consequently, it allowed the appeal and decreed the suit filed by the plaintiffs and directed the defendant No.1 to pay a sum of Rs.51,612/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of suit till the date of realization.
10. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the First Appellate Court, the defendant No.1 has filed this appeal.

11. This appeal was admitted to consider the following substantial question of law:
"Whether the lower appellate Court was justified in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court having regard to the relationship of the parties coupled with the fact that second defendant-daughter, after deserting her husband was living with the first plaintiff and the money spent being the NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 money paid to the doctor towards treatment given during pregnancy?"
12.

The learned counsel for the defendant No.1 submitted that the expenses incurred by the plaintiff was not upon the defendant No.1 but was upon the defendant No.2 and therefore, it was incumbent upon the plaintiffs to prove that the defendant No.1 had agreed to reimburse the expenses incurred for the treatment of defendant No.2.
He submitted that defendants No.1 and 2 were not residing together and therefore, the expenses incurred for the treatment of the defendant no.2 cannot be imposed upon the defendant No.1.
He further contended that the plaintiff No.1 did not enter the witness box but he has given power of attorney to his brother to enter the witness box and depose.
He contended that the PW1 did not know the transactions between the parties and therefore was not a competent witness.
PW2 was not a person who was present at the time of the alleged understanding between the plaintiffs and the defendant No.1 and therefore, he too was not a competent witness.

He further submitted that the First Appellate Court committed an error in allowing the appeal in-part and directed the defendant No.1 to pay a sum of NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 Rs.51,612/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of suit till the date of realization.
13. Per contra, learned counsel for the plaintiffs remained absent and therefore this Court did not have the benefit of his submissions.
14. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the defendant No.1 15.
The fact that the defendant No.2 was treated as an inpatient between 04.03.1991 to 06.03.1991 at KLE Hospital, Belgaum is substantially established by Ex.P10.
The defendant No.2 was thereafter referred to Wanloss Hospital, Miraj where she underwent a surgery and medical termination of pregnancy.

This is also evidenced by Ex.P39 which is the inpatient bill issued by Wanloss Hospital,
Miraj.
Therefore, there are sufficient documents to indicate that defendant No.2 was admitted in the said hospitals for the purpose of undergoing a procedure.

sentences.text: Ex. P53
is a challan dated 25.03.1991 which indicates that a sum of Rs.21,555/- was deposited for purchasing the pacemaker.

Thus, as rightly held by the trial - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 Court and the First Appellate Court, there was sufficient evidence to establish that the defendant No.2 underwent a procedure for termination of pegnancy and also for a pacemaker implantation.

The documents also clearly indicate that the plaintiffs had spent a sum of Rs.51,612/- for the treatment, operation and medicine expenses of the defendant No.2.
17.
The defendant No.1 denied the expenses incurred as well as the fact that the defendant No.2 had undergone this medical procedures.
He admitted that he did not spend anything for the treatment of his wife after marriage.
However, it was incumbent upon the plaintiffs to establish that the defendant No.1 had agreed to pay the expenses incurred by the plaintiffs on defendant No.2.

The fact that the defendant No.2 had thereafter initiated proceedings in Crl.Misc.No.566/1993 and also lodged a complaint against the defendant No.1 alleging offence under Section 498A of the IPC makes it more than clear that the defendants No.1 and 2 were not in good terms and that there was no love lost between them.
However, the First Appellate Court has held that the defendant No.2 was admitted for treatment between 15.11.1989 to April, 1991.

It - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 was incumbent upon the defendant No.2 to establish that the defendant No.1 was residing with her or that she was residing with defendant No.1 between 15.11.1989 and April, 1991 or that the matrimonial relationship between them was alive.
However, the entire records does not disclose that the defendants No.1 and 2 were not living together as husband and wife from the year 1989 till the year 1991.
It is undoubtful that the defendant No.1 as the husband of the defendant No.2 had a continuing responsibility to maintain the defendant No.2 until her death or until she is divorced and remarried.

But, if defendant No.2 has separated from defendant No.1 and is living with her parents, she was bound to justify as to why she was living away from the defendant No.1, to claim the expenses of her treatment.
Therefore, it can be safely held that defendant No.2 had abandoned defendant No.1.
No reason are cited as to why she had separated from defendant No.1.
This apart, the suit was not filed by defendant No.2 but by her father and a relative.

18. In the absence of any documentary or oral evidence to show that defendant No.1 had agreed to reimburse the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3206 expenses incurred, it cannot simply be assumed that defendant No.1 had agreed to reimburse the expenses.

sentences.text: The First Appellate Court held that in matters of this nature, there cannot be a stricto sensu contract but a contract has to be gathered from the circumstances.

The First Appellate Court also held that the defendant No.1 was employed as a Government servant serving in the Telecom Department as Lineman and therefore, he could have claimed reimbursement of the expenses incurred for the defendant No.2.
If that was the case, the plaintiffs ought to have handed over the bills to the defendant No.1 to make a claim before his employer and recover the expenses.

However,
the plaintiffs have not chosen to do so, but have launched a suit to recover the said sum from defendant No.1.
The conduct of the plaintiffs therefore is unbecoming and borders on an attempt to harass defendant No.1.
Therefore, the substantial question of law framed by this Court is answered against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendant No.1.
Consequently, this appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and decree of the First Appellate Court is set aside and the suit filed by the plaintiffs is dismissed.
